titleText.es: El 40% de las instalaciones de OpenBSD conducen a un ataque de tiburones. Es el único bug de seguridad que tienen.
titleText.en: 40% of OpenBSD installs lead to shark attacks. It's their only standing security issue.
titleText.noteEn: The title text turns the comic's escalating upgrade disaster into a joke about OpenBSD's strong security reputation: its only remaining 'security issue' is supposedly sharks.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; helps desarrollarse mean ‘to develop or progress’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: With a project, plan, or situation as the subject, desarrollarse describes how it unfolds or progresses without naming an outside doer.

example.es: La reunión se desarrolla con calma.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Desarrolla is the present form used with one project or situation. With se, it describes that subject unfolding over time.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; helps hacerse mean ‘to become’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: With a describing word, hacerse can present a gradual or noticeable change in the subject's state.

example.es: Los días se hacen más largos.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Hacen normally means ‘they make,’ but se hacen followed by a description can say that several things become or grow that way.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: dual; using two systems (in arranque dual)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In computing, arranque dual is a setup that lets one machine start either of two installed operating systems.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: a short time; soon (inside dentro de poco)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After dentro de, poco names an unspecified short interval from now. The full phrase dentro de poco means ‘soon’ or ‘before long.’

cardDefinitions.answerEn: I will end up; I will remain (with me)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Quedaré is the future form for the speaker. With me and a describing word, it states the resulting or continuing condition.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to leave; to keep (something in a state)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Dejar can mean not changing something, especially when the following words describe the state in which it remains.

example.es: Voy a dejar la puerta abierta.
example.en: I'm going to leave the door open.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: it was; used to be (a past state)
at the; begins al principio, ‘at the beginning’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Al is the required contraction of a + el. With principio it locates something at the beginning of a process or period.

example.en: At the beginning it was difficult.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: beginning; start (as part of al principio)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Al principio places a state or event at the beginning of a process, story, or period.
El sobremesa is a shortened form of el ordenador de sobremesa. In other contexts, la sobremesa can instead mean the conversation and time spent at the table after a meal.

example.es: Uso un sobremesa en la oficina.
example.en: I use a desktop computer at the office.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: With causa, perdida forms causa perdida, a situation no longer expected to succeed.

example.es: Todos creen que es una causa perdida.
example.en: Everyone thinks it is a lost cause.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: As a noun in computing, el portátil is a laptop. As an adjective, portátil means portable.

example.es: Mi portátil necesita una batería nueva.
example.en: My laptop needs a new battery.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Dejarán is the future form used for they. With an object and en paz, it means that they will stop bothering that person.

example.en: They will leave us alone tomorrow.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; links dejar to paz in dejar en paz
cardDefinitions.noteEn: En is required inside the expression dejar a alguien en paz, meaning to leave someone alone or stop bothering them.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: alone; in peace (inside dejar en paz)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Paz normally means peace. In dejar a alguien en paz, the full expression means leaving that person alone or no longer bothering them.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: we reach; we arrive (an awaited-event form)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Lleguemos is the special form used for we after expressions such as hasta que when the arrival is still in the future.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; begins con vida, ‘alive’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Con vida describes a person or animal as still living, often after danger or rescue.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: you will do again (with a + action)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Volverás is the future form for informal singular you. Followed by a and an unchanged action verb, it says that the action will happen again.
After nunca, más extends the negative into the future: nunca más means ‘never again.’

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can you say that a person or thing becomes or gradually grows a certain way?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the matching form of hacerse followed by the word that describes the new state.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The short marker and hacer form change with the subject: me hago, te haces, se hace, nos hacemos, and so on. The describing word matches the person or thing in number and, when its form changes, gender.

example.es: Las tardes se hacen más cortas.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that a quality keeps increasing over time?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Put cada vez más before the describing word; repeat y más for extra emphasis.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Cada vez más means ‘increasingly’ or ‘more and more.’ The emphatic form cada vez más y más stresses that the change continues. The final describing word still matches what it describes.

example.es: Las calles son cada vez más estrechas.
example.en: The streets are getting narrower and narrower.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: What is the Spanish expression for a computer setup that can start either of two operating systems?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Arranque is the startup or boot process. Dual says that two systems are available; the user chooses one when the computer starts.

example.es: Configuré un arranque dual con Linux.
example.en: I set up dual boot with Linux.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say “at the beginning” or “at first”?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Al combines a + el. Al principio can locate something at the beginning of a process, or contrast an initial situation with what happened later.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you describe a situation that seems hopeless and no longer worth trying to save?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The literal words are ‘a lost cause.’ Perdida is feminine because it describes causa. The expression can refer to a project, effort, or situation, not only a social cause.

example.es: El viejo motor es una causa perdida.
example.en: The old engine is a lost cause.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone is lucky or has good luck?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the matching form of tener followed by suerte.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish builds this with tener, ‘to have’: tengo suerte, tienes suerte, tenemos suerte. Do not use ser before suerte for this meaning.

example.en: We were lucky with the weather.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you tell or say that someone should be left alone and no longer bothered?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of dejar, identify the affected person, and add en paz.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The affected person can appear as me, te, lo, la, nos, or another object form. En paz stays fixed: déjame en paz means ‘leave me alone.’

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone is still alive after danger or when found?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The phrase can follow verbs such as volver, encontrar, rescatar, or salir. Natural English usually uses the adjective ‘alive’ rather than translating con separately.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something will never happen again?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Nunca supplies ‘never’ and más extends it to ‘again’ or ‘anymore.’ If the phrase follows a verb that already has no before it, Spanish keeps both negatives.

example.en: I never want to see it again.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: OpenBSD is an operating system known for emphasizing security; the comic invents shark attacks as its absurd remaining security problem.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The worsening computer repair ends with the characters in shark-filled water. The title text pretends that 40% of OpenBSD installations cause shark attacks and calls that the system's only standing security issue.

regions.labelEs: MIENTRAS SE DESARROLLA UN PROYECTO, LAS PERSPECTIVAS DE ÉXITO SE HACEN CADA VEZ MÁS Y MÁS PEQUEÑAS.

applications.exampleEs: SE HACEN CADA VEZ MÁS Y MÁS PEQUEÑAS
applications.explanationEn: Se hacen presents a gradual change in the plural perspectivas, and pequeñas is feminine plural to match them.

applications.exampleEs: CADA VEZ MÁS Y MÁS PEQUEÑAS
applications.explanationEn: Cada vez más marks an increasing degree, and y más repeats the increase for emphasis before the final description.

excludedUnits.rationale: This is the panel's elapsed-hour number, not Spanish vocabulary; Vision read the handwritten zero as the letter O.

regions.labelEs: VALE, DEBERÍA PODER TENER UN ARRANQUE DUAL CON OPENBSD DENTRO DE POCO.

excludedUnits.rationale: This is the unchanged proper name of an operating system, not Spanish vocabulary.

applications.explanationEn: Debería presents the ability as expected, while poder remains in its unchanged dictionary form.
Poder is itself unchanged after debería, and tener stays unchanged after poder to name the ability.
Arranque names the computer's startup process and dual says that two operating systems can be selected.
Dentro de introduces a future interval, and poco makes that interval an unspecified short time.

excludedUnits.rationale: This is the panel's elapsed-hour number, not Spanish vocabulary.

regions.labelEs: ME QUEDARÉ CONTENTO SI PUEDO DEJAR EL SISTEMA TAL Y COMO ESTABA AL PRINCIPIO.

applications.explanationEn: Me and quedaré form the first-person future of quedarse, and contento names the resulting state.
Quedar keeps its complete dictionary stem and adds -é for what the speaker will do; me marks the pronominal verb separately.
Si introduces a condition treated as possible, and puedo uses the ordinary present form.
Puedo changes for the speaker, while dejar stays in its unchanged dictionary form.

applications.exampleEs: TAL Y COMO ESTABA AL PRINCIPIO
applications.explanationEn: Tal y como introduces the exact earlier state, and estaba al principio supplies that complete comparison.
Estaba uses the imperfect because it presents the system's earlier condition as a continuing background state.
Al is a + el, and principio names the initial point of the repair process.

excludedUnits.rationale: This is the panel's elapsed-hour number, not Spanish vocabulary.

regions.labelEs: BUENO, EL SOBREMESA ES UNA CAUSA PERDIDA, PERO CREO QUE PUEDO ARREGLAR LOS PROBLEMAS QUE SURGIERON EN EL PORTÁTIL.

applications.explanationEn: Causa is feminine, so perdida matches it; together the words label a situation that now seems hopeless.
Puedo changes for the speaker, while arreglar stays in its unchanged dictionary form.
Que connects problemas to the added information supplied by surgieron.
Surgieron presents the problems' appearance as a completed past event, not a continuing background state.

excludedUnits.rationale: This is the panel's elapsed-hour number, not Spanish vocabulary.

regions.labelEs: SI TENEMOS SUERTE, LOS TIBURONES NOS DEJARÁN EN PAZ HASTA QUE LLEGUEMOS A AGUAS POCO PROFUNDAS.

applications.explanationEn: Si presents a genuinely possible condition, and tenemos stays in the ordinary present form.
Tenemos changes for we, while suerte completes the fixed way of describing luck.
Nos names the affected people, dejarán is the plural future action, and en paz completes the fixed expression.
Dejar keeps its complete dictionary form and adds -án for what they will do.
Hasta que introduces the limit, and lleguemos uses the special awaited-event form because the arrival has not happened yet.

regions.labelEs: SI VOLVEMOS CON VIDA, NO VOLVERÁS A ACTUALIZAR NADA NUNCA MÁS.

applications.explanationEn: Si introduces the possible condition, and volvemos uses the ordinary present form even though the return is still in the future.
Con vida forms the fixed description for returning while still alive.
Volverás changes for informal singular you in the future, a links it to actualizar, and actualizar stays unchanged.
Volver keeps its complete dictionary form and adds -ás for informal singular you in the future.
Nunca supplies the negative and más extends it into ‘again’ or ‘anymore.’

applications.exampleEs: NO VOLVERÁS A ACTUALIZAR NADA NUNCA MÁS
applications.explanationEn: No stays before the verb phrase while nada and nunca más add matching negative information after it; Spanish keeps all of these negatives together.
